subject: Business Models
title: Escrow and Guarantees
description: Learn Escrow and Guarantees in one minute.

hook.text: Upwork holds the client's payment until the freelancer delivers. Neither side risks getting cheated.

buildup.text: Escrow removes the 'who pays first' dilemma. The platform holds the money as a neutral party.

discovery.text: Airbnb's $1 million host guarantee protects against property damage. The guarantee enables stranger transactions.

twist.text: Guarantee claims are often denied on technicalities. The promise of protection matters more than its delivery.

climax.text: Escrow and guarantees make impossible transactions routine. Without them, the sharing economy collapses.

punchline.text: Hold the money, guarantee the outcome. Trust is engineered, not assumed.

quiz.question: What problem does escrow solve in marketplaces?

details.summary: Escrow services hold buyer payment until the transaction is completed satisfactorily, protecting both parties from fraud. Marketplace guarantees like money-back promises further reduce transaction risk..
details.whyItMatters: Escrow and guarantees remove the trust barrier that prevents marketplace transactions. By holding funds and offering recourse, marketplaces make strangers comfortable enough to transact, enabling markets in categories like freelancing, real estate.
takeaways: Escrow holds buyer payment until the seller delivers as promised
Money-back guarantees reduce buyer risk and increase purchase confidence
Trust mechanisms enable high-value transactions between complete strangers

faq.question: How does marketplace escrow work?
faq.answer: The buyer pays the marketplace, which holds funds. The seller delivers the product or service. The buyer confirms satisfaction or raises a dispute. If satisfied, funds are released to the seller. If disputed, the marketplace arbitrates..

faq.question: What are the costs and limitations of escrow systems?
faq.answer: Escrow delays seller payment, affecting cash flow. Operating escrow requires financial licensing in many jurisdictions. Defining satisfactory completion can be subjective, especially for services. Escrow systems add transaction friction that may reduce conversion for low-value purchases.
